title: Read any piece
summary: Tap any piece, yours or theirs, and its card shows under the board while its reach shows on the board. Hold a piece for a quick look, and let go to close it.
problem: Today a tap on an enemy piece gives a refusal. A touch player cannot read an enemy piece. A player cannot see how an enemy piece moves, why the Archer gives check from far away, or why a Guard cannot be taken.
idea: One card for every piece, in a fixed place under the board: figure, name, one line, what it can do now and a small rule example. The engine draws the reach on the board in shapes of their own, so a reading never looks like your move. On a short phone the card folds to one row, and Rules opens the full page.

borrows.what: Every enemy attack shows before it happens, so a loss is never a surprise. Here: their Archer's shots over your pieces.
Press and hold a card to see it large. Here: the figure lifts and its card rises, then goes when you let go.
Each piece carries a tiny move diagram. Here: a 5 x 5 rule example that the engine works out.
A '?' mode that turns every tap into a question. Here: option C, the lens.

options.name: Tap to read
options.summary: A tap reads any piece in the fixed context area. Close, Escape or the next tap ends it.

options.name: Hold to read
options.summary: Hold a figure: it lifts, its reach shows and a card rises over the context area. Let go and it all goes. The action bar stays clear.

options.name: The ? lens
options.summary: A Read button turns on a mode: names on the King Down pieces, and every tap reads. No move plays.

recommendation: A and B together. A tap is easy to find and works with the keyboard; a hold is the fast path, and it can read a marked enemy without a move. Keep C out: it adds a mode that a player must leave.
notes: Look at 'rest' first: the fixed context area before a read. The quiet tip shows until the first read, then goes.
Look at 'tap': you are in check from far away. Their Archer's card says why, and the arcs show the shot over your pawn on f2.
Look at 'hold-target': your Beast is selected, and a hold reads their Ogre, a marked target. Nothing plays. A tap on the same square bites. The live demo and the video do this with real taps.
'frozen': you froze their Archer. It cannot move or shoot next turn, but it still gives check. Thin ice sights show the squares where it still gives check.
'short-tap' and 'short-hold': a phone with its browser bars (390 x 700). The card folds to one row. Rules opens the rule example. The hold card never covers the action bar.
Every reach, every ice sight and every rule example comes from the engine (KD.legal), for your pieces and for theirs. The demo writes no rule.
Live: play White against the Casual computer. Tap reads, hold reads, I on the keyboard reads. A tap, a drag or Enter on a marked target plays the move.

Limits: no hover reading with a mouse (a click, a 400 ms hold or the I key reads). The lesson button and Menu only show a message. In the app, the tip shows in three games at most. A phone held sideways is not part of this demo.
